what: Every subcommand against representative inputs and expected exit codes
why: A decoder that passes its own tests can still fail at the command line.
method: E:/oadec-work/verify-2026-09-14/smoke.py (all 12 subcommands, 28 media clips, the committed fixtures, empty and random input); smoke_fix.py re-ran the cases whose first run used a wrong tool syntax; smoke_final.py is the same matrix with the branch-head binary
reading: 212 cases, 56 not as the matrix expected. 46 are head cuts that verify and decode rightly call faulty (a TrueHD head ends inside an access unit, an E-AC-3 head starts inside a frame); 4 used an option atmos_info 1.1 does not have, and on re-run every DAMF set and every tagged ADM file passed both atmos_info versions and bwf_info; 1 was eac3-ecpl-inject correctly refusing a stream without coupling, and on a 384 kbit/s stream it converted 3305 of 3305 frames, verify was clean and Dolby's decoder played it. 5 were defects: info and oamd exited 0 on an empty file and on random bytes, and decode exited 0 on an empty file. All five are fixed on the branch. At the branch head: 212 cases, 51 unexpected: the 46 head cuts, the 4 atmos_info 1.1 syntax cases and the coupling refusal, nothing else. 10 cases changed exit code, each by a fix: info and oamd on empty and random input 0 to 2, decode on empty input 0 to 2 and on random input 7 to 2, emdf on the configuration 4 head 7 to 0 (AC-3 framing), oamd on E-AC-3 2 to 0. At 1a7e10c, after the changes of the review loop, the same 212 cases gave the same exit codes as at 3418cdf, 51 unexpected and all of them the designed ones. At b00f490, after round 4, W4 and G4, the same 212 cases gave the same 51 designed unexpected ones, and 13 exit codes changed against 1a7e10c, every one emdf or oamd on a clip cut inside a frame or an access unit, 0 to 7
